# Add Investor staff members

## Problem statement

The staff family has no member that manipulates the **market row** itself: every ability so far buffs income, reputation, costs, incidents or hand capacity. The Investor introduces a market-shaping role — one **free market re-roll per turn** that is **biased toward the business type where the Investor is employed** — giving players a reason to invest coins in scouting favourable offers rather than accepting the first row they see. Moving the Investor to a different business costs an action point, so the ability is a deliberate positioning decision rather than a free upgrade.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a market-manipulation tool that rewards placing an Investor next to the business type they are trying to grow.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants a coin-free way to dig for a missing synergy piece (e.g. a Food business while running a Food cluster).

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a free market re-roll each turn while an Investor is employed, so that I can look for a better offer without paying the escalating re-roll cost (MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ).
- As a Main Street player, I want the Investor's free re-roll to be 75% likely to surface cards relevant to the business it is employed at, so that placing it near my cluster meaningfully improves my odds.
- As a Main Street player, I want to move the Investor to a different business for one action point, so that I can retarget the bias at a cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Investor card exists in the catalog.** A new `staff-investor` row is added to `src/card-data.csv` (feature flag `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, bias `0.75`, no hand slots, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`), with a tier assignment, cost, ongoing cost and description consistent with the staff ladder and the ×100 coin scale; it flows into the general market via the existing tier-gated staff deck (`createStaffDeck`).
- **AC2 — One free re-roll per turn.** While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform **one** coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it **advances the per-turn escalation counter** (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- **AC3 — Relevance bias.** On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a **75% chance** to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`; event `targetSynergy`/effect; staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap with the hosting business's synergy types) — the free `refillSingleRowMarket` path is parameterised so the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- **AC4 — All staff relocation costs an action point.** Relocating a hired staff member from one business to another is exposed as a player action and consumes **1 action point** for **all** staff (the existing `placeStaffOnBusiness` placement is action-free today and must be action-gated when used as a relocation; the initial placement at hire time remains part of the hire action). The move respects `allowedBusinessTypes` and employment-slot capacity, is undoable, and is persisted.
- **AC5 — UI & tooltips.** The market re-roll button/tooltip and the Investor's staff tooltip/employed-staff summary surface (a) whether the free re-roll is still available this turn and (b) the 75% relevance bias; the button label/tooltip reflect the coin-free state when available and the escalated cost when not. Wording stays consistent with the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename if that lands first.
- **AC6 — Undo, save/load and determinism.** The per-turn free-re-roll flag, the per-turn escalation counter it increments (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`), the Investor's location and any bias state participate in undo/redo (`snapshotAction`) and in `MainStreetStateSerialize` (serialize + migrate backfill + deserialize), so mid-turn reload preserves both availability and the escalated next price; the bias draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed ⇒ same-game determinism holds.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit/integration tests cover: catalog + CSV contract; free re-roll is coin-free, once per turn, resets at `WeekStart` and advances the escalation counter; the 75% relevance bias (deterministic with a seeded RNG) and its random fallback; movement action cost + undo + save/load round-trip; and existing re-roll/discount/action-economy tests are updated for the new card and counts.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the Main Street rules docs (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`) and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC9 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **New mechanic, not just data.** The relevance bias and the free re-roll are new engine behaviour; they must be additive and must not change existing behaviour when no Investor is employed.
- **Single source of truth for re-roll cost.** The free re-roll must not silently bypass `refreshMarketCost()`; the paid path and its escalation (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) remain authoritative for non-free re-rolls, and the free re-roll must increment the same per-turn escalation counter.
- **Reuse the market composition model.** `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) enforces the ≥1-business row composition; the biased draw must preserve that invariant.
- **Placement/employment invariant.** `business.employedStaff` and `staff.employedAtSlot` are kept in sync by the existing placement helpers; the move action must route through them.
- **Art drift guard.** `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` requires every unique card name to map to dedicated art or a documented pending-art target, and forbids growing the art-less baseline (currently 79). The Investor therefore needs a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite **or** an explicit, producer-approved pending-art entry (see `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`).
- **Coin scale.** All coin values are ×100 (per the integer-economy migration); the Investor's cost/ongoing cost must follow the existing staff ladder (`MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z`).

## Existing state

- **No Investor exists** anywhere in the repo or worklog (searched `investor`, case-insensitive, excluding `node_modules`/`dist`); only the unrelated `Investor Bonanza` event fixture appears in a test.
- **Market re-roll is already action-free** (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 "Free operations: Market re-roll/refresh"), so "without using an action" means the Investor's re-roll is free of **coins** as well; the normal re-roll costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` (500, escalating per `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).
- `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) builds the row: 3 slots, ≥1 business, at most 1 upgrade / 1 event / 1 staff, drawing via `state.rng` (seeded).
- `refreshMarket(state)` / `refreshMarketCost(state)` / `canRefreshMarket(state)` live in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; discounts come from `refreshCostDiscount` staff and the Negotiator skill.
- **Staff placement is free today**: `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`) explicitly consumes no action/coins; `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand`/`removeStaffFromBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:674/692`) wrap it in `snapshotAction`. There is currently **no** player-facing "move staff" action.
- Staff card fields live in `StaffCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts:330`), parsed in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` (CSV columns incl. `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `allowedBusinessTypes`); the catalog currently holds **25** staff rows.
- Per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`) are reset in `executeWeekStart` (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`).
- Card-count baselines that will shift when a staff row is added: `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (`toHaveLength(25)`), `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` (166 / 174 totals), `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- **CSV/catalog:** add `staff-investor` with a new bias column (e.g. `marketRelevanceBias = 0.75`) plus a free-re-roll marker (e.g. `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`), no `handSlotsAdded`, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`, and a description in the existing "reduces X by Y" house style.
- **Types/parsing:** add the new optional `StaffCard` fields and parse them in `MainStreetCardsTemplates` (numeric column for the bias; boolean/flag column for the ability).
- **Engine:** add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` state (reset at `WeekStart`), a `canUseFreeMarketReroll`/`useFreeMarketReroll` pair (coin-free, action-free, once per turn) that **increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn`**, and a `refillSingleRowMarket`-compatible biased draw parameterised by the hosting business's synergy types + `0.75`.
- **Movement:** add a move-staff engine function + command that charges 1 action via the existing weekly action budget for **any** staff relocation, reusing `placeStaffOnBusiness` semantics (adding the action gate at the command layer).
- **Serialization:** add the new state field to serialize, migrate (backfill `false`/`0`) and deserialize.
- **UI:** market re-roll button/tooltip shows the free re-roll availability; staff tooltip/employed-staff summary states the free re-roll + 75% bias; a move-staff affordance that costs an action.
- **Docs & art:** update the rules/catalog/progression docs; add the Investor sprite (or a documented pending-art entry) and regenerate `card-art-map.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `staff-investor` row (new bias column + free-re-roll flag; tier, cost, ongoing cost, description).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard.freeMarketRerollPerTurn?` / `StaffCard.marketRelevanceBias?` (+ doc comments).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new CSV columns into the new fields.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — free re-roll path (`canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`), bias-aware `refreshMarket` variant, and cost/label reporting.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — parameterise `refillSingleRowMarket` with an optional relevance pool; keep the default path unchanged.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the per-turn free-re-roll flag.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new per-turn state field (and serialized-state entry).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate backfill (and deserialize) the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — move-staff engine function + command (1 action), free-re-roll command.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — helpers to detect the employed Investor and its hosting business synergy types.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — free-re-roll button state, tooltip and availability text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — employed-staff summary / staff tooltip line for the new ability.
- `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Investor art (or a documented pending-art entry).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — free re-roll, relevance bias, movement cost.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row + ability cell.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — catalog baselines.
- `tests/main-street/` — new `investor-staff.test.ts` (free re-roll, bias, movement) plus updates to `refresh-market.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts` and any staff-count assertions.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open): escalates the paid re-roll cost; its appendix explicitly leaves "free re-rolls do not advance the escalation counter" as an assumption to settle with this item.
- `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (in-progress): touches the same market re-roll button/tooltip; coordinate wording and the free-re-roll affordance.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — "Some staff cards should add action points" (completed): establishes the weekly action budget and the staff card UI/action patterns the movement cost builds on.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): most recent end-to-end staff-ability implementation (CSV → engine → docs → tests); follow its structure.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — "Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card" (open): owns the art-less baseline; the Investor raises the drift-guard question.
- `MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL` — "Add a charity shop" (completed): precedent for adding a card and updating the catalog/count baselines.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decision (free = coins-free, escalation-advancing):** because market re-roll is already action-free, "free re-roll, without using an action" means **no coin cost and no action cost**, but the free re-roll **advances** the per-turn escalation counter. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias definition):** "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" = shares a synergy type with the hosting business; businesses/community-space by `synergyTypes`, events by `targetSynergy`, staff by `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias application):** the 75% applies per drawn slot with a random fallback; the entire row is not a single 75% roll. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (no stacking):** multiple Investors still grant a single free re-roll per turn (avoids a degenerate multi-Investor loop). *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (movement scope):** **all** staff relocation costs an action; the initial placement at hire time is unchanged. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Risk (scope creep / existing behaviour):** the re-roll cost item and the rename item touch the same button; implementing the free re-roll without advancing the counter would desynchronise the displayed price, and newly action-gating **all** staff relocation changes an existing free operation (and its tests). Mitigation: keep `refreshMarketCost()` authoritative, increment the shared counter on the free re-roll, and update the staff-placement tests in the same change.
- **Risk (determinism/tests):** adding a card changes seeded deck draws and several fixed-count baselines; many fixtures inline counts. Mitigation: update the documented baselines and count assertions in the same change, and cover the bias with a seeded-RNG test.
- **Risk (art drift guard):** a new art-less card fails `card-art.test.ts`; either supply a sprite or get a producer-approved pending-art entry, otherwise the item is blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`.
- **Risk (save compat):** forgetting the migrate backfill leaves old saves with `undefined` and a throwing/NaN free-re-roll gate. Mitigation: backfill in `migrateSerializedState` and assert a round-trip.
- **Risk (balance):** a free re-roll per turn plus a 75% biased row is a strong information advantage; cost/tier may need balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`). Mitigation: pick a mid/premium tier and revisit after playtest.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-09-30; answered by the producer 2026-09-30).**

- **Q1 (free re-roll semantics):** "The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's 'free re-roll' free you from, and does it stack/interact with the escalating cost (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`)? Options: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack; (b) one coin-free re-roll per Investor (stacks); (c) the free re-roll also resets the escalation counter; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** one coin-free, action-free re-roll per turn; it **does advance the escalation counter**; multiple Investors do **not** stack.

- **Q2 (relevance definition & application):** "How is 'relevant to the type of business they are currently located at' defined, and how does the 75% apply? Options: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback; (b) relevant by exact business name only; (c) the **whole row** is 75% likely to be relevant; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** as recommended — **(a)** shared synergy type, applied per drawn slot, with random fallback.

- **Q3 (movement cost & scope):** "Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? Options: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free; (b) **all staff** relocation costs 1 action; (c) the move is free but limited to once per turn; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** **(b)** — **all** staff relocation costs 1 action.

**Secondary assumptions (not asked in Round 1, to keep to the ≤3-question limit):**

- **Card economics (default):** `staff-investor` is a generalist (all synergy types), `handSlotsAdded: 0`, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125 — mirroring the tier-5 specialist band (Financial Advisor). *Recorded as an assumption; the producer may re-balance.*
- **Art (default):** add a dedicated 1024×1024 Investor sprite and regenerate `card-art-map.json`; if art cannot be produced, request a producer-approved pending-art entry so the drift guard passes.
- **Rename coordination (default):** implement the free-re-roll affordance on the existing re-roll button so it survives the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename without conflicting wording.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-09-30):** The free re-roll and relevance bias are **not** implemented anywhere (repo + worklog search). The re-roll is already action-free and coin-costed (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`); `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) is the single composition point; staff placement is action-free (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`). This item is therefore a **new mechanic + card + docs + art** change, not a data-only change.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ** – Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution (open)
- **MS-0MUE2U21C0007BKL** – [test-failure] upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts > animates the transfer from the drop location and plays the upgrade SFX (beginDrag timeout) — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ability, ac4, ac5, acceptance, action (+430 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: abilities, ability, acceptance, action, add (+332 more)

# Storyline Coverage Analytics in Monte Carlo Harness

## Problem Statement

The Monte Carlo balance harness (MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts) currently tracks card ownership, market offers, and economy history across simulation runs, but has no visibility into storyline event coverage. Storyline events — which form branching chains with accept/reject choices — are a key game mechanic, yet the harness cannot report how often storylines fire, how deeply their chains progress, whether cycles appear, or what impact storyline choices have on win rates. This leaves the balance team blind to storyline-related balance issues.

## Users

- **Balance team / game designers**: Want to understand whether storylines are contributing positively to the game (e.g., do "Accept" choices correlate with higher win rates? Do certain storylines trigger too or too rarely?).
- **Content designers**: Want to verify that all storylines are being exercised in simulation and that chains progress reasonably (not dead-ending too quickly or cycling excessively).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline fire frequency**: The harness reports how many runs and what percentage feature each storyline (`storyline-economy`, `storyline-health`, `storyline-labor`, `storyline-restaurant`, `storyline-tax`), derived from event-choice transcript records captured during simulation runs.

2. **Chain depth tracking**: For each storyline event encountered, the harness tracks how far the chain progresses (number of consecutive chain cards pushed), reported per storyline as a distribution (mean, median, max depth) across runs.

3. **Cycle detection**: The harness detects and counts cycle occurrences (tax → tax-error → tax-inquiry → tax, per `storyline-manifest.json` edges with `cycle: true`), reporting cycle frequency per storyline and per run.

4. **Win-rate impact of choices**: For each storyline with choices (flu-outbreak, popular-menu, recession, strike-service, tax, tax-error, tax-inquiry), the harness computes the win-rate differential between "Accept" and "Reject" choices — similar to existing M2 win-rate delta pattern.

5. **Integration with existing analytics**: Storyline analytics are exposed as new functions in the balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) following the same pattern as existing metrics (G1–G8, M1–M7), with graceful degradation when storyline data is absent.

## Constraints

- **Non-blocking**: This is a deferred enhancement; it must not change existing Monte Carlo harness behaviour (strategies, termination, output format for non-storyline fields).
- **Graceful degradation**: All new storyline metrics return `null` when event-choice data is not available in run summaries (consistent with existing M4/M6/G4/G6/G7 patterns).
- **Builds on existing transcript recording**: The harness already has a lazy `recordMainStreetEvent` call path via `require('./MainStreetTranscript')`; the extension should extend this path to capture event-choice data into a new field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`.
- **No UI changes required**: Output is analytical (JSON/CSV), consistent with existing harness output.

## Existing State

- Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) runs simulations with strategies (market-greedy, demo-greedy, greedy, banking-greedy, random) and records `MonteCarloRunSummary` per seed.
- The harness already records `cardsOwned`, `marketOffers`, and `economyHistory` on run summaries (Phase 1 data).
- Storyline events with choices are resolved in-engine; `recordStorylineResolution` in `MainStreetStoryline.ts` emits `event-choice` transcript events.
- The Monte Carlo harness has a try/catch wrapper for `recordMainStreetEvent` that silently ignores failures when no recorder is wired.
- Storyline manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`) defines 5 storylines, 14 edge transitions, and 1 cycle group.
- Balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) has 8 global metrics (G1–G8) and 7 card metrics (M1–M7) with graceful degradation patterns.

## Desired Change

1. **Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary`** with a new field capturing event choices encountered during a run (event ID, choice made, chain depth at that point).
2. **Wire transcript recording** in the Monte Carlo harness so that event-choice events are captured (not just ai-action events).
3. **Add storyline analytics functions** to the balance engine:
   - `computeStorylineFireFrequency(runs)`: percentage of runs per storyline.
   - `computeChainDepthStats(runs)`: depth distribution per storyline.
   - `computeCycleStats(runs)`: cycle frequency per storyline and per run.
   - `computeChoiceWinRateDelta(runs, eventId)`: win-rate difference between Accept vs Reject.
4. **Export storyline metrics** from the balance engine barrel file.
5. **Add tests** covering all new analytics functions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary` interface; wire transcript recording for event-choice events.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — Barrel file for new storyline metrics exports.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — New analytics module for storyline-specific metrics.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — Tests for storyline analytics functions.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — Reference for storyline definitions and cycle edges (read-only).

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — write storylines (epic, completed): The parent epic that shipped the storyline system.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed): Provides the manifest data model.
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** — Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed): Provides storyline naming and feedback mechanics.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — Static validator & npm gate (completed): Validates storyline integrity.

# Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects

## Problem statement

The generalised storyline option model (`StorylineOption`) currently supports
only a label, a single successor, and an apply/skip effect policy. Content and
engine authors cannot express options that are only available when the player
can afford them, that branch to different successors based on game state, or
that carry their own extra effects. The game-agnostic seam
(`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) was explicitly designed to grow into these
semantics, and this capability was deliberately deferred from the
`write-storylines` epic as speculative until now.

## Users

- **Engine/content authors** — need richer per-option semantics (affordability
  gates, state-based branching, extra effects) without bypassing the
  game-agnostic seam or hand-writing bespoke engine code per card.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need the extension to stay declarative,
  serialisable, statically validatable, and portable to the core engine.
- **Players** — should only be offered choices they can actually take, and
  should have their decisions reflected accurately in coins/reputation.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — must keep selecting legal, presented options so
  headless games never stall or pick a hidden/unaffordable branch.

### Example user stories

- "As an engine author, I want to gate an option behind a coin/reputation cost,
  so the choice only appears when the player can afford it."
- "As a content designer, I want an option's successor to depend on coins or
  reputation, so one choice can lead down different branches."
- "As a content designer, I want an option to apply an extra effect on top of
  its apply/skip policy, so choices can have their own consequences."
- "As a developer, I want invalid cost/condition data to fail the validator, so
  mis-authored storylines cannot ship."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional
   `cost`, `extraEffect` (`{ coins?: number; reputation?: number }`), and
   ordered `conditionalSuccessors` (`{ when: { field: 'coins'|'reputation';
   op: '>='|'<='|'>'|'<'|'=='; value: number }; successorId }`) fields. Omitting
   all three preserves today's behaviour exactly — verified by the existing
   legacy-equivalence and C1 regression harness passing unchanged.
   *Metric: unit tests + existing regression harness pass with zero behavioural deltas.*

- **Cost gating.** An option whose `cost` exceeds the player's current
   coins/reputation is **omitted** from the presented option list; available
   options are computed and stored with the pending choice so resolution
   indexing, transcript tokens, and save/load stay stable. Selecting an
   affordable option deducts the declared cost as an additional payment,
   independent of its `effectPolicy`, and applies any `extraEffect`.
   *Metric: unit tests assert exact coin/reputation deltas, omission, and stable indexing.*

- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` is evaluated in order;
   the first matching rule wins, and the option's `successorId` is the fallback
   when none match. Above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match
   fallback cases are covered, including succeeding-card push.
   *Metric: unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.*

- **Static validation & schema.** The validator and manifest schema reject
   invalid new data — negative/empty cost, malformed conditions (unknown field
   or op, non-numeric value), and dangling conditional successors — while the
   shipped CSVs validate cleanly and the doc-drift test passes.
   *Metric: validator unit tests with broken fixtures + clean run on shipped content.*

- **AI / Monte Carlo integration.** `decideEventChoice` (and the generalised
   AI selection path) chooses only among presented/affordable options and
   accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas; the regression and Monte Carlo
   harnesses run to completion without stalls.
   *Metric: AI policy tests + regression/Monte Carlo harness green.*

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (option model, resolution
   lifecycle, roadmap), the migration notes in `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
   and the CSV column reference in `src/README.md` (confirming the new
   semantics remain programmatic, not CSV-authored).
   *Metric: doc-drift test passes; reviewer confirms docs match code.*

- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
   *Metric: full test suite green.*

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only (producer decision Q1=A).** Extend the
  in-memory model, engine resolution, validator, and schema. Keep the legacy
  CSV at the two-way Accept/Reject shape; do **not** add CSV columns for the
  new semantics.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only
  field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas. Arbitrary callbacks are out of
  scope here — see the follow-up work item below.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics must live behind
  `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and keep the future core-engine extraction
  viable (pure/declarative data, no Main-Street globals baked in beyond the
  injected template registry).
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** A cost
  may specify either or both; an option is available only when *all* specified
  costs are affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are
  removed from the presented list, not shown greyed out.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted from the
  player in addition to the option's apply/skip effect policy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.

## Existing state

- `StorylineOption` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) = `{ label, successorId,
  effectPolicy }`. `CompiledStoryline` wraps an ordered option list.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` compiles legacy `hasChoices` /
  `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId` into `[Accept, Reject]`, and supports
  explicit multi-way lists via `registerStorylineOptions(eventId, options)`.
  `getStorylineOptions(event)` is pure (no state) and is used by callers,
  the validator, and the graph exporter.
- `resolveStorylineOption(state, event, option)`
  (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) applies `effectPolicy` and pushes
  `option.successorId`; `resolveEventOption(state, optionIndex)`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) indexes the option list, records the
  transcript, and drives `pushChainCard`.
- `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) returns a binary
  `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta` / `reputationDelta`,
  `projectEventCoinDelta`, `eventSeverity`, and successor severity.
- Validation lives in `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`; the manifest/schema
  in `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`; docs in
  `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (§2 model, §3 lifecycle, §9 seam, §10
  roadmap).
- `PendingEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) currently stores
  `{ event, chosenOption, resolved }`.

## Desired change

Extend the option model and resolution path so that:

1. Options declare an optional affordability `cost`; the presented option list
   is filtered to affordable options before the dialog/AI sees it, and the
   filtered list is stored with the pending choice.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered
   `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time using the
   declarative predicate vocabulary.
3. Selection deducts `cost`, applies `extraEffect` independently of
   `effectPolicy`, and pushes the first matching conditional successor (or the
   default `successorId`).
4. The validator, schema, and graph/manifest export understand the new fields;
   the AI policy operates over the presented option list.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extend `StorylineOption` with `cost`,
  `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors`; add a `Condition` type.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Filter options by affordability, apply cost +
  extra effects, resolve conditional successors; expose a state-aware
  accessibility accessor alongside the pure `getStorylineOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Store the presented/available option list on
  `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses the stored
  presented list; update logging/transcript for cost and extra effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` selects only among
  presented options and accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — Validate cost/condition/effect data and
  conditional successor targets.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`
  — Represent and validate the new option metadata in the manifest/graph.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — Document the extended option model and
  resolution semantics; update the seam/migration notes.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — New/extended coverage.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV` — **write storylines** (completed epic; parent context).
- `MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV` — **Storyline model & extraction seam** (completed; the
  generalised `StorylineOption` this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP92O9002772U` — **Storyline behaviour regression harness** (completed;
  the byte-for-byte regression guard).
- `MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6` — **Static validator & npm gate** (completed; the
  validator this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ` — **Storyline authoring helper CLI** (completed).
- `MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0` — **Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema**
  (completed; manifest/schema this extends).
- `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N` — **Support arbitrary callback conditions/successors in
  storyline options** (follow-up, medium priority, `discovered-from` this item).
- Roadmap entry: `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10.

## Risks

- **Option-index drift.** Filtering options changes the index space; the
  pending-choice list must be frozen at draw time or the UI, AI, and transcript
  can disagree. *Mitigation:* store the presented list on
  `PendingEventChoice` and resolve by index into it.
- **AI divergence.** `decideEventChoice` is currently binary; a generalised
  selector that ignores affordability/cost could pick a hidden option or stall.
  *Mitigation:* route AI through the same presented list; cover with
  regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **Manifest/schema churn.** Adding optional fields can break the graph export
  or doc-drift test. *Mitigation:* keep new fields optional and update schema,
  exporter, and docs in the same change.
- **Scope creep.** Arbitrary callbacks, CSV authoring, and per-option animation
  are explicitly out of scope; the callback escape hatch is tracked separately
  as `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface.** How far should this change reach?
  - Answer (producer): **A** — extend the in-memory model + engine resolution +
    validator/schema only, programmatically via `registerStorylineOptions`;
    keep the legacy CSV at two-way Accept/Reject. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Cost-gated semantics.**
  1. What gates eligibility?
     - Answer (producer): **coins and/or reputation**. Source: interactive reply.
  2. When unaffordable, omitted or shown disabled?
     - Answer (producer): **omitted**. Source: interactive reply.
  3. Is the cost deducted on selection in addition to apply/skip?
     - Answer (producer): **yes**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Conditional successors & per-option extra effects representation.**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — declarative, serialisable data
    (`extraEffect` + ordered `{ when, successorId }` rules with `successorId`
    fallback). Additionally: create a **medium-priority follow-up work item**
    to add arbitrary callbacks. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up created as
    `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

### Assumptions

- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  legacy/card behaviour must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- Because a pending choice blocks all player actions, the set of affordable
  options is stable between draw and resolution; storing the presented list on
  the pending choice makes this explicit and save/load-safe.
- Cost deduction that drops coins or reputation to zero triggers the normal
  loss checks (no special-casing).

# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-10-01, interactive reply): **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**; **Q2 = A (epic, decomposed into vertical slices)**;
**Q3 = A (curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

Storylines can only be authored today by hand-editing `src/card-data.csv` or by
driving the transaction-safe `storyline-author` CLI, and the graph can only be
viewed as a generated Mermaid/JSON artefact. Content designers therefore cannot
*see* the arc they are editing, cannot discover links and dangling targets
visually, and cannot make a guided, validated edit in one place. The seed
roadmap entry (`docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10) calls for a visual
storyline authoring editor that reads `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`,
renders the graph interactively, and writes edits back through the same
transactional, self-validating author operations.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — see a storyline's shape at a glance,
  inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename, retarget a
  link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV internals.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — trust that every edit goes through one
  validated, transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync
  with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write
  a dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool that is excluded
  from the game build and reuses the existing author API, so it adds no runtime
  dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

1. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain (no new runtime
   dependency). It is a development tool and must not be included in the game
   build.
2. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and
   node selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

3. A Node-side bridge that exposes the existing author operations
   (`add-card`, `link`, `set-storyline` from `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`)
   and the validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) to the editor.
4. Every edit is **previewed and validated before writing**; an invalid result
   leaves `src/card-data.csv` untouched and surfaces actionable errors.
5. On an accepted edit, regenerate `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` via the existing
   `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` generator so the existing drift test stays
   green.
6. Concurrency guard: refuse to overwrite the CSV if it changed on disk outside
   the editor session (content hash / mtime check) and ask the author to reload.

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

7. Edit an existing card's fields: name, effect text, coin/reputation deltas,
   `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
   `storylineTitle`.
8. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
   pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

9. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
   group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
10. Documentation in `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (and the `src/README.md`
    script/column references) covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow,
    validation and artefact regeneration.
11. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test
    for the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor` starts the tool
   from the repo root on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain with no new
   runtime dependency; the command is documented in `docs/main-street/storylines.md`.
   Verified by a test that invokes the entry point (dry/`--help` mode) and asserts
   it exits 0.
2. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the committed
   manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`): all nodes and edges
   appear, choice cards are visually distinct, storyline grouping and cycle
   edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its links/metadata. Covered by a
   browser test.
3. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the committed manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and the JSON
   schema.
4. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   listed in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through
   `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (`add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`). A test
   asserts no editor module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through that
   module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
5. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
6. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`; `npm run storylines:graph --
   --format json --check` and the doc-drift test pass. Covered by a test.
7. **Concurrency guard** — if `src/card-data.csv` changed on disk since load,
   the editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
8. **Game build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the
   production game bundle; verified by a build/test assertion (e.g. the editor
   entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts` graph).
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `src/README.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single write path** — the editor must reuse the existing transactional,
  self-validating author operations; it must not introduce a second way to edit
  `src/card-data.csv`.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing Vite/`vite-node`/Vitest/
  Playwright toolchain.
- **Deterministic artefacts** — the manifest/mmd generators must stay
  timestamp-free; the existing drift test must continue to pass.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Backward compatibility** — CSV schema/column order and legacy
  `hasChoices`/accept/reject semantics must be preserved; the C1 regression
  harness must stay green.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to
  players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — richer option semantics (conditional/cost-gated effects,
  `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9`) are out of scope; the editor edits today's two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Manifest + schema** — `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` (generated,
  deterministic, 5 storyline ids, nodes/edges/cycles) and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` (draft-07, `additionalProperties:
  false`).
- **Graph export** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` with
  `npm run storylines:graph -- --format mermaid|json` and a `--check` drift
  guard; committed `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`.
- **Transactional author API** — `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (CLI
  `npm run storylines:author`, `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`): builds the
  edited CSV in memory, loads it through the typed model and validates **before**
  writing; `--dry-run` and `--csv <path>` supported.
- **Validator** — `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` (`validateStorylines`,
  `formatStorylineReport`), cycles informational, `--fail-on-cycle` opt-in.
- **Model/seam** — `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` (`compileStorylineFromEvent`,
  `getStorylineOptions`, `registerStorylineOptions`, `resolveStorylineOption`,
  `pushChainCard`); CSV authoring keeps the two-way representation.
- **Stack** — Vite + Phaser + Electron; scripts run under `vite-node` because
  the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query.
- **Gap** — no interactive editor; the only graph view is the static generated
  Mermaid/JSON; nobody can edit through a UI. Even the strongest surrounding
  visualisation item (`MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`) only renders the committed `.mmd`
  to SVG in the docs build.

## Desired change

1. **Host a local editor** — `npm run storylines:editor` serves an in-repo dev
   page backed by a small Node-side API bridge over the author/validator/graph
   modules.
2. **Interactive viewer** — render the manifest graph with storyline grouping,
   choice/plain distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom/select.
3. **Guided editing** — edit card fields and add/relink cards through forms that
   preview the diff and validate before write.
4. **Stay in sync** — regenerate the committed mmd/manifest after accepted edits
   and guard against concurrent external CSV edits.
5. **Document and test** — authoring walkthrough for the editor, unit tests for
   the bridge/view-model and a browser round-trip test.

**Recommended slice order for planning** (epic, per Q2 = A): (S1) host +
read-only viewer; (S2) write bridge + preview/validate; (S3) curated edit forms;
(S4) storyline management + docs/tests polish. The `plan` skill will formalise
the children and dependencies.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — **new** entry point (`vite-node`).
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` (or a Vite dev-server plugin) —
  **new** host + API bridge.
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — **new** thin wrapper over
  `storyline-author.ts`, `validate-storylines.ts`, `storyline-graph.ts`.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/` (or `tools/storyline-editor/`) — **new** editor
  UI (HTML entry + TS view-model/graph rendering).
- `package.json` — add the `storylines:editor` script.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — **edit** tooling/authoring sections.
- `src/README.md` — **edit** script and CSV-column references.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor.test.ts` — **new** bridge/view-model tests.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor.browser.test.ts` — **new** Playwright UI test.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`, `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`
  — generated artefacts (regenerated on accepted edits).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — "write storylines" (epic, completed/in_review) — the
  parent that shipped the validator, graph/manifest export and authoring helper
  this editor builds on; its roadmap entry in
  `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10 is the seed for this work item.
- **MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ** — "Storyline authoring helper CLI" (completed) — the
  transactional write API the editor wraps.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — "Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema"
  (completed) — the manifest/schema/generator the viewer reads.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — "Static validator & npm gate" (completed) — the
  validation feedback surfaced in the editor.
- **MS-0MUMP92O9002772U** — "Storyline behaviour regression harness" (completed)
  — must stay green after editor changes.
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — "Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the
  docs build" (in-progress) — adjacent read-only visualisation; potential
  overlap in rendering conventions.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** — "Extend storyline options with conditional and
  cost-gated effects" (open) — future option model; explicitly out of scope here,
  but the editor's form model should not preclude it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk (epic)** — "visual editor" can balloon into a full graph editor;
  *mitigation:* slice order (viewer → bridge → forms → management) and keep
  direct-manipulation graph editing out of the accepted first increments.
- **Write-path risk** — a browser UI could grow its own CSV writer;
  *mitigation:* AC4 enforces the author-API-only path with a test.
- **Concurrency risk** — external CSV edits during an editor session could be
  overwritten; *mitigation:* AC7 hash/mtime guard.
- **Build-leak risk** — the editor entry could be bundled into the game;
  *mitigation:* AC8 build exclusion test.
- **`?raw` import constraint** — the card model imports the CSV via Vite `?raw`,
  so the bridge must run under `vite-node`/Vite middleware rather than plain
  Node; *mitigation:* the host builds on the existing toolchain (Q1 = A).
- **Assumption** — "storylines" means the Main Street incident event-chain
  system; no other storyline implementation exists in the repo.
- **Assumption** — the editor is a local developer/content tool; hostability
  outside a repo checkout is not required.
- **Assumption** — the editor's first increments target the shipped two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model; multi-way/programmatic options remain out of scope.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Answered (producer, round 1 — 2026-10-01, interactive reply)

- **Q1 — Delivery form / host.** Where should the editor live and how is it
  launched? Options: (A) in-repo local web tool; (B) in-game developer overlay;
  (C) standalone Electron tool. **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer:
  A — in-repo local web tool** launched with `npm run storylines:editor`, built
  on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain and writing only through the
  existing author API. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Work-item shape & first increment.** Options: (A) epic decomposed into
  vertical slices; (B) single feature; (C) read-only MVP only.
  **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer: A — epic**, decomposed into
  vertical slices (viewer → write bridge → edit forms → storyline management +
  docs/tests). The work item's `issueType` was set to `epic`. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Editing interaction model.** Options: (A) curated form/guided editor;
  (B) direct-manipulation graph editor; (C) both (form first, graph later).
  **Recommended:** (A). **Final accepted answer: A — curated form/guided
  editor**, with diff/preview and validate-before-write; no free-form canvas
  manipulation. Source: interactive reply.

### Answered (repo research — no interactive reply needed)

- **Q0 — Write path.** The editor must use the existing transactional author
  API (`src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`: `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`)
  and must not add a second CSV edit path. Evidence: the author module already
  validates in memory before writing; the seed states "write edits back through
  the same transactional, self-validating author operations".
- **Q0b — Artefacts.** After an accepted edit, regenerate
  `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
  `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` via
  `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`; the existing `--check` drift guard and
  doc-drift test must pass. Evidence: `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §5/§7.
- **Q0c — Stack constraint.** The editor host must run under Vite/`vite-node`
  because the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw`
  query. Evidence: the `storyline-author`/`storyline-graph`/`validate-storylines`
  CLIs are all `vite-node` entry points.

- None. All blocking questions are answered (Q1–Q3, producer); the epic scope

# Fix stale `example-games/main-street/` paths in docs after the `src/` migration

**Headline.** The game repo's docs still point at the pre-migration `example-games/main-street/` layout; remap every remaining reference under `docs/` to `src/`, reword the one migration-plan sentence that must name the old layout, and add a Vitest guard that fails if the stale prefix is ever reintroduced.

## Problem statement

The Main Street source tree moved from `example-games/main-street/` to `src/`, but 33 references across 10 files under `docs/` still use the old prefix. Anyone following a doc link or command ends up at a path that no longer exists, and there is no test preventing further drift.

## Users

- **Game developer / maintainer** — follows a doc reference (e.g. `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md`) and needs it to resolve to the current `src/` file.

# Intake Brief: Re-evaluate Upgrade Costs/ROI After the Five-Turn Payback Rebalance

**Work item:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 (Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns)
**Recommendation R1:** Re-evaluate upgrade costs/incomeBonus so upgrades clear the ~5-turn payback opportunity cost.

## Headline

The five-turn payback rebalance (MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3) left upgrades severely under-valued: 9 of 39 upgrade cards show 0% adoption on the after-state, and the expensive tier (cost 7–14) is universally rejected by the greedy AI. This task re-derives upgrade `cost` and `incomeBonus` values so upgrades are genuinely worth purchasing in a meaningful share of runs.

## Problem statement

Businesses now recover their cost in ~5 turns, making each turn of play more economically tense. However, an upgrade must (a) require a parent business to already be owned, and (b) spend 3–14 coins on top of the business's remaining payback, so upgrades rarely clear the opportunity cost before the run ends. With `incomeBonus` values set proportionally to upgrade cost (e.g. cost 9 → bonus 300), the ROI `incomeBonus × horizon − cost` is positive only when `horizon` is large — but runs last ~10–12 turns on average, and the AI's planning horizon (floor=5, cap=25) means cheap upgrades barely clear positive-NPV. The expensive tier never does.

## Users

- **Player** — wants building decisions to carry real economic tension, including meaningful upgrade choices (e.g. "Should I invest in my Diner or bank these coins?"). Currently, upgrades feel like dead ends.
- **Producer / designer** — wants a diverse economy where investment (upgrades) is a viable strategy alongside banking and business expansion.
- **Developer** — wants the changes to be small, targeted, and reversible, backed by before/after Monte Carlo evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** The current upgrade pick rate (M1: purchases / market appearances) and M5 adoption (upgrade purchases / parent purchases) are recorded from the after-state canonical profile (200 seeds, 60 max turns, `mc-balance`, greedy). Results documented in the work-item description.
2. **Changes applied.** Upgrade `cost` and/or `incomeBonus` values in `src/card-data.csv` are adjusted so that at least the cheap upgrades (cost ≤5) reach a measurable pick rate and the expensive tier reaches a non-trivial pick rate. **No engine-rule changes.**
3. **Before/after evidence.** The canonical Monte Carlo profile is re-run post-change; pick rates and adoption rates are recorded as a before/after comparison. Win-rate ladder Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard is preserved.
4. **Full test suite passes** with the new values (`npm test`).

> Standard criteria also met: at least one testing/validation criterion (AC2), documentation updated where relevant, and full suite green (AC4). CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Constraints

- **No engine-rule changes** (card-data.csv is the only lever).
- **Integer ×100 economy** — costs and bonuses are integer coin-cent units.
- **Preserve the win-rate ladder** (Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard) as the primary gate.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Community-space pricing, event pricing, and business income are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups.
- **Budget discipline:** Changes must not materially shift win rates (±0.05 on Medium) — upgrades represent a small share of total income.

## Existing state

### Post-rebalance after-state (commit 8b8fe46, current dev tip — card-data unchanged since rebalance)

**200 seeds / 60 turns / Medium / greedy Monte Carlo (canonical profile):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Runs with ≥1 upgrade | 31.0% (62/200) |
| Aggregate M1 pick rate (all upgrades) | 8.18% (88/1076 appearances) |
| Upgrade share of all purchases | 8.43% (89/1056) |
| Aggregate M5 adoption (upgrade vs parent owns) | ~10.50% |

### Upgrade performance (after-state, sorted by M1 pick rate)

**Top performers (M1 ≥ 15%):**
| Upgrade | Cost | incomeBonus | M1 Pick Rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upg-gourmet-truck | 3 | 150 | 24.0% |
| upg-gaming-lounge | 7 | 200 | 23.8% |
| upg-gourmet-deli | 4 | 150 | 19.2% |
| upg-bistro | 3 | 100 | 18.8% |
| upg-bespoke-tailor | 4 | 100 | 17.9% |

**Mid performers (M1 5–15%):**
upg-readers-cafe (17.4%), upg-patisserie (16.7%), upg-roastery (12.1%), upg-wellness-retreat (12.1%), upg-tea-lounge (12.0%), upg-resort-spa (11.5%), upg-smoothie-bar (11.5%), upg-grand-fountain (11.1%), upg-adventure-park (10.3%), upg-community-hub (9.4%), upg-vintage-shop (9.1%), upg-garden (8.7%), upg-orchard (8.7%)

**Low performers (M1 0–5%):**
upg-designer-store (7.7%), upg-fast-food (7.4%), upg-drive-in (7.1%), upg-fitness-center (6.7%), upg-garden-center (6.5%), upg-bread-factory (6.5%), upg-toy-warehouse (6.5%), upg-dry-cleaners (5.7%), upg-imax (4.8%), upg-health-center (3.7%), upg-wellness-center (3.2%), upg-private-medical-center (3.1%)

**Never picked (M1 = 0%):**
upg-home-improvement, upg-salon, upg-museum, upg-medical-center, upg-grand-bakehouse, upg-restaurant, upg-multiplex, upg-luxury-retreat, upg-dental-clinic (9 upgrades)

### AI upgrade scoring formula

```
score = incomeBonus × horizon − cost
horizon = clamp(ceil((winThreshold - score) / scorePace), 5, 25)
```

For a 0-turn-horizon floor of 5:
- Cost 3, bonus 100 → score = 500 − 300 = **+200** (positive, competitive)
- Cost 9, bonus 300 → score = 1500 − 900 = **+600** (positive at floor, but expensive)
- Cost 14, bonus 550 → score = 2750 − 1400 = **+1350** (positive but very high cost)

The expensive upgrades' high `incomeBonus` values make them look attractive on paper, but their high `cost` means they rarely appear in the market before the game ends, and when they do, the AI prioritises cheaper alternatives with better cost-adjusted returns.

## Desired change

1. **Raise `incomeBonus` or lower `cost` for the 0%-tier upgrades.** Target: lift the top cheap upgrades to ≥20% M1 pick rate and the expensive tier to ≥5% M1 pick rate.
2. **Adjust the cheap tier upward modestly** if they fall below the target.
3. **Document every change with rationale.**
4. **Re-run Monte Carlo and compare.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Upgrade row edits (`cost`, `incomeBonus`).
- `tests/main-street/business-payback.test.ts` — May need update if cost/income changes affect business payback (unlikely, as upgrades are a separate family).
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/card-metrics.ts` — M5 `computeUpgradeAdoption` may need base-ID normalisation (instance-suffixed `cardsOwned` vs. base card IDs).
- `docs/main-street/` — Update balance documentation with before/after results.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns (parent context).
- **MS-0MUQUBJQF009PTZ0** — Re-tune compensating balance levers (deferred upgrade pricing to this item).
- **MS-0MUQUBKNE007NYR8** — Further-balancing recommendations (R1: upgrade re-pricing).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Premise nuance (research finding).** The "≤1% of runs" claim in the further-balancing report appears to refer to per-upgrade individual run-participation (many are ≤1%). However, the aggregate picture is more nuanced: 31% of runs pick ≥1 upgrade, and the cheap tier already shows 16–24% M1 pick rates. Only the expensive tier (cost 7–9+) is truly broken at 0%. This may narrow the scope.
- **Metric definition note.** The M1/M5 functions (`computePickRate`, `computeUpgradeAdoption`) compare base card IDs against instance-suffixed `cardsOwned` entries (e.g., `biz-laundromat-1`). The baseline should either (a) normalise IDs by stripping `-N` suffixes or (b) use instance IDs consistently. This is a known pattern in `MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`.
- **No engine-rule changes.** Changes are card-data only; the scoring formula and horizon remain unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk.** If producer wants community-space or event pricing adjustments too, record as linked follow-ups.
- **Budget discipline.** Upgrade income is a small share of total income, so changes should have minimal impact on overall win rates. The win-rate ladder should be preserved.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (success metric & scope — OPEN QUESTION):** *What is the success threshold, and which upgrade tiers need fixing?*
  - **Recommended: B** — Focus on the expensive tier (cost ≥7) where 9 upgrades hit 0% adoption. Cheap upgrades already perform at 16–24% M1.
  - Option A: Fix all upgrades, target ≥5% M1 for every upgrade.
  - Option B: Fix only expensive tier (cost ≥7), target ≥5% M1.
  - Option C: Accept current cheap-tier performance; only fix expensive tier to ≥10% M1.

  **Answer (producer):** B- **Q2 (change scope — OPEN QUESTION):** *What is in bounds for changes?*
  - **Recommended: A** — `cost` + `incomeBonus` in card-data.csv only.
  - Option A: Cost + incomeBonus only.
  - Option B: Also adjust AI horizon parameters (AI_HORIZON_FLOOR, scoring formula).
  - Option C: Also adjust guardrail preservation requirements.

  **Answer (producer):** A- **Q3 (premise accuracy — OPEN QUESTION):** *The data shows 31% of runs pick ≥1 upgrade (aggregate M1 = 8.18%). The "≤1% of runs" claim in the report refers to per-upgrade individual participation. Should the goal be to lift ALL upgrades above the current floor, or only the broken tier?*
  - **Recommended: B** — The expensive tier (9 upgrades at 0%) is the real problem; cheap upgrades already meet a reasonable baseline.

  **Answer (producer):** B
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MTR39XO6002CBB1** – Events income/costs should be shown on the business cards (open)

- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac4, accept, acceptance, affect, aggregate (+275 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, adjust, adjustments, affect (+251 more)

# Intake Brief: Level-2 Upgrade Prerequisite Gate Blocks Expensive-Tier Adoption

**Work item:** MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M (Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance)
**Producer decisions:** Q1→(a), Q2→(a), Q3→(a) — see Appendix.

## Headline

On the canonical greedy Monte Carlo profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, Medium) four level-2 upgrades — `upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat` — still sit at **0% M1 pick rate** and **0% M5 adoption**, because the AI almost never advances their parent businesses to level 1. This item re-tunes the *level-1 prerequisite cards'* `cost` values (card-data only) so the level-2 tier becomes reachable through the intended two-step chain, while leaving the level gate itself (US-19) intact.

## Problem statement

Level-2 upgrades are structurally gated: the AI emits a `buy-upgrade` action only when a business satisfies `biz.name === card.targetBusiness && biz.level === requiredLevel && biz.level < biz.maxLevel` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`). The four level-2 upgrades carry `requiredLevel: 1`, so they need a parent already at level 1. The greedy AI advances only ~7–13% of parents to level 1, so the intersection of *(level-2 card in market) × (parent at level 1) × (affordable)* is effectively zero. Cost/`incomeBonus` changes on the level-2 cards themselves cannot move adoption (Experiment B preserved 0% M1), because the binding constraint is upstream: too few level-1 parents exist.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the late-game investment tier to be a real choice (e.g. "My Diner is doing well — should I push it to a full Restaurant?"). Today the most powerful upgrades in the pool are unreachable in practice.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the level-2 chain to function as designed (a two-step progression reward) and to be demonstrably reachable in the canonical simulation, without weakening the chain design.
- **Developer** — wants a small, reversible card-data change with before/after Monte Carlo evidence, consistent with the parent item's card-data-only precedent.

User story: *As a player running a profitable Bakery, I want a path to the Grand Bakehouse to be realistically attainable, so that investing in a favourite business pays off over a full run.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline and before/after evidence captured.** On the canonical profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, `greedy`, sweep Easy/Medium/Hard — command below), record M1 pick rate for the four level-2 upgrades and M5 adoption for the four parents (Bakery, Diner, Cinema, Day Spa) and their level-1 prerequisites, both before and after the change, commit-stamped in the work-item description.
2. **Target reachable.** All four level-2 upgrades reach **≥5% M1** on the canonical Medium profile, with a non-zero absolute purchase count.
3. **Leading indicator rises.** Level-1 parent adoption (M5 for `upg-patisserie`/`upg-bread-factory`, `upg-bistro`/`upg-fast-food`, `upg-imax`/`upg-drive-in`, `upg-resort-spa`/`upg-wellness-center`) measurably increases versus the captured baseline.
4. **Gate and chain preserved.** The four level-2 upgrades keep `requiredLevel: 1`, and `canPurchaseUpgrade()` still enforces level equality (PRD-milestone-2 US-19 AC2/AC3 unchanged). No engine-rule changes in this item.
5. **Ladder preserved.** Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ordering is retained and the Medium win-rate moves within ±0.05 of the pre-change baseline.
6. **Testing and validation.** A Vitest test asserts the canonical card-data invariant (the four level-2 upgrades have `requiredLevel: 1`) and the M1/M5 metric computation used for the before/after evidence; the full project test suite passes with the new values.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` are updated where the re-derived costs are referenced; code comments touched by the change are updated.

## Constraints

- **Card-data values only** (`src/card-data.csv`, and only `cost` / `incomeBonus` fields). No engine-rule, AI-priority, or deck-mechanic changes in this item.
- **Preserve US-19** (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md`): level-2 upgrades keep `requiredLevel: 1`; `canPurchaseUpgrade()` equality is unchanged; the two-step chain described in `card-catalog.md` remains valid.
- **If the ≥5% target is unreachable** within card-data-only tuning, raise a **separate** engine/deck work item (e.g. a per-card market weight/copies column or a shared upgrade-deck `copies` change) rather than expanding this item's scope.
- Adjustments must be minimal and reversible, with commit-stamped before/after evidence.
- Win-rate ladder Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard must be preserved.
- No CHANGELOG.md edits (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state

Canonical profile: 200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy, Medium (current `dev` tip). Six upgrades at **0% M1 / 0% M5**:

| Upgrade | Level req. | Parent | Card `cost` | Outcome |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| `upg-museum` | 0 | Art Gallery (rare) | 700 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-dental-clinic` | 0 | Dentist (rare) | 700 | 0% (7.1% when cost→300) |
| `upg-grand-bakehouse` | 1 | Bakery | 900 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-restaurant` | 1 | Diner | 1400 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-multiplex` | 1 | Cinema | 1400 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-luxury-retreat` | 1 | Day Spa | 1400 | 0% M1 |

Parent purchase counts across 200 runs: Bakery 44, Diner 38, Cinema 34, Day Spa 7. Level-1 parents (of 200): Bakery ~4, Diner ~8, Cinema ~4, Day Spa ~4.

Prior experiments (recorded on the work item): removing the gate lifts the four level-2 upgrades to 2.9–10.3% M1 (isolates the gate); aggressive level-2 cost/bonus cuts leave them at 0% M1; boosting level-1 prerequisite `incomeBonus` barely moves level-1 adoption because the AI's Priority-3 upgrade purchase is unconditional; lowering `upg-dental-clinic` cost 700→300 alone reached 7.1% M1. **Cost (affordability) is the only score-independent card-data lever not yet fully tested.**

Reproduce the baseline:

```bash
npx vite-node src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts \
  --sweep --seeds 200 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 60 \
  --sweep-strategies greedy --sweep-difficulties Easy,Medium,Hard \
  --out results/level2-gate-before.json
```

M1/M5 are derived from `MonteCarloRunSummary.marketOffers` / `cardsOwned` via the balance-analysis API (`computePickRate`, `computeUpgradeAdoption`; see `docs/main-street/balance-analysis-api.md`).

## Desired change

Re-tune the **level-1 prerequisite cards'** `cost` values down (and their `incomeBonus` only where cost alone is insufficient) so that materially more parents reach level 1, and, if required, reduce the level-2 cards' `cost` so an existing level-1 parent can afford the second step. The gate stays in place; the chain is preserved. Concretely, candidates are the expensive level-1 branches — `upg-bread-factory` (700), `upg-fast-food` (700), `upg-imax` (700), `upg-drive-in` (700), `upg-wellness-center` (900), `upg-resort-spa` (900) — plus the level-2 `cost`s (`upg-grand-bakehouse` 900; `upg-restaurant`/`upg-multiplex`/`upg-luxury-retreat` 1400). Evidence must show which lever did the work.

If card-data tuning proves insufficient to reach ≥5% M1, document the shortfall and create the follow-up engine/deck work item; do not change engine rules here.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — adjust `cost` (and `incomeBonus` where justified) for the six level-1 prerequisite cards and, if needed, the four level-2 cards; do **not** change `requiredLevel`.
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` — canonical profile runner (sweep mode, `mc-balance` seeds, 60 turns).
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — run loop; source of `marketOffers` / `cardsOwned` per-card metrics.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `buy-upgrade` action generation (level-gate matching) and Priority-2/3 selection; read-only reference for the gate semantics.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `canPurchaseUpgrade()` and the level/`displayName` mutation on upgrade application.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — US-19 (Multi-Level Upgrade Chains) constraint; read-only.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — multi-level upgrade chain description and cost references.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — upgrade cost formula used to re-derive values.
- `core/src/balance-cards/` — balance cost-curve helpers (used by `run-balance-cards`), if re-derivation uses them.
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts` — existing balance-card tests; extend for the invariant test.
- `src/scripts/balance/baseline-blocks.ts` — baseline/target blocks used by guardrail checks.

## Related work

- MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance (source item; `blocked`, card-data-only precedent).
- MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns and economy re-tune (completed; introduced the payback regime).
- MS-0MUQUBK1B006EODZ — After-state Monte Carlo, guardrails and baseline (completed; canonical profile definition).
- MS-0MUQUBJQF009PTZ0 — Re-tune compensating balance levers (completed).
- MS-0MUVPB1UE004UUBI / MS-0MUUYI950004TG7F — upgrade ownership/regression tests (completed; test precedent).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** – Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI) (completed)
- **MS-0MUML5X1L008LT8Z** – Implement Physiotherapist rename across all files (completed)
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** – Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, affordable, alone, already (+134 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, action, alone, already, bakehouse (+117 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: action, adoption, affordable, alone, already (+115 more)

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4.md`.

## Assumptions

- The M1/M5 formulas and canonical profile remain stable; comparisons are like-for-like at the same seed/strategy/difficulty.
- The greedy AI's unconditional Priority-3 upgrade purchase is unchanged (no AI edits in scope), so affordability and market co-occurrence are the operative levers.
- `200 seeds` gives adequate resolution for a ≥5% target (5% ≈ 1.5 purchases of ~30 appearances; small-n noise is acknowledged and the leading indicator plus absolute counts are reported alongside).

## Risks

- **Small-n noise**: M1 on ~30 appearances is coarse; a ≥5% target could pass/fail by chance. *Mitigation:* report absolute purchase counts and the level-1 leading indicator; consider a larger seed count for the decisive run.
- **Card-data tuning insufficient**: if level-1 adoption cannot be lifted enough without an engine/deck change, the ≥5% target may be unreachable in scope. *Mitigation:* explicit escalation path to a separate engine work item (documented, not silent scope creep).
- **Ladder regression**: cheaper upgrades may shift win rates. *Mitigation:* AC4 ladder check with the ±0.05 Medium band.
- **Scope creep**: other zero-adoption cards (`upg-museum`, `upg-dental-clinic` with rare parents) invite broadening. *Mitigation:* keep them out of scope; log as separate work if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (fix direction, given US-19).** Which approach should this item implement? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Preserve US-19 and the two-step chain; lift level-2 reachability by re-tuning level-1 prerequisite costs (card-data-only, matching the parent's "cost + incomeBonus only" scope); escalate to an engine/deck change as a separate work item only if the ≥5% target is unreachable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (acceptance criteria).** Keep the proposed targets *plus* a level-1 leading-indicator AC? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Yes — keep the proposed ACs and add the level-1 leading indicator. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (scope boundary).** Card-data values only, or allow a minimal engine/deck change in this item? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Card-data values only first; spin off any engine change as a new work item. Source: interactive reply.

Research note (agent): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` US-19 AC2/AC3 require `requiredLevel: 1` and `canPurchaseUpgrade()` level equality; the original "Experiment A" (`requiredLevel 1→0`) would break a committed PRD AC and the chain, so option (a) was adopted. Experiment C's null result is explained by the AI's unconditional Priority-3 purchase, which makes `incomeBonus` score-independent and leaves `cost` (affordability) as the viable card-data lever.
